Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) rather than raw Decimal operations.
  Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling functions like line_total/invoice_total to match rounding and normalization conventions. Wrap unit prices with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round the final result with round_money.
- [rb-0020] Use Decimal constants for monetary rates and fixed fees: Define percentage rates and fixed fees as module-level Decimal constants, never floats, to avoid rounding drift.
  Declare `RATE = Decimal("0.029")` and `FIXED = Decimal("0.30")` at module level and compute `round_money(amount * RATE + FIXED)`. Floats are rejected by the project's `to_money`, so all monetary math must stay in Decimal.
- [rb-0013] Reuse existing money helpers for currency math: When implementing monetary functions, delegate to the repo's existing to_money/round_money helpers rather than raw float arithmetic.
  Search sibling modules (invoice.py, adjustments.py) for established money utilities and error types before writing new code. Using to_money/round_money and BillingError kept the implementation consistent with the codebase and passed hidden tests on the first try.
- [rb-0022] Reuse existing money helpers instead of reimplementing rounding: When a repo already has to_money/round_money utilities, build new monetary functions on top of them rather than writing fresh Decimal logic.
  Before implementing any amount-handling function, grep for existing money helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO, CENT) and import them. This keeps rounding policy and float-rejection behavior consistent across modules and avoids subtle mismatches with hidden tests.
- [rb-0005] Normalize money inputs before sign checks: Convert unit_price via the project's to_money helper before comparing against ZERO, so strings/Decimals are handled consistently.
  Run raw price inputs through the existing money conversion helper (e.g. to_money) first, then compare the normalized Decimal to ZERO for the negative check. This accepts flexible input types while keeping validation correct.
- [rb-0018] Follow sibling module conventions for state, time, and audit: Match existing patterns in the codebase (ensure_utc for timestamps, BillingError('invalid_state', ...) for wrong state, audit.record with event name and fields).
  Before implementing, read sibling modules like invoice.py and payments.py to copy conventions: use ensure_utc(at) for stored times, raise BillingError('invalid_state', f'payment {payment.id} is {payment.status}') for invalid transitions, and call audit.record with a descriptive event name plus relevant fields including idempotency_key.

item.title: Reuse project money helpers for currency math
item.description: When computing monetary values, use the repository's existing to_money/round_money helpers instead of raw Decimal arithmetic.
item.content: Search for existing money utilities (e.g., round_money, to_money, ZERO) and apply them so rounding and type coercion match project conventions. This keeps new functions consistent with sibling code like invoice totals.

item.title: Grep for the target symbol and its dependencies before implementing
item.description: Locate the stub, its dataclass fields, and any existing tests in one pass to infer exact expected behavior.
item.content: Run grep across source and tests for the function name plus relevant field names (e.g., plan_price, period_days) to find usage examples and expected return types before writing code.

item.title: Verify edge cases with a quick script after implementing
item.description: After passing tests, run a small ad-hoc script covering rounding boundaries and type variations to confirm correctness.
item.content: Exercise cases like non-divisible prices (10/3 -> 3.33), small values, and string-vs-Decimal inputs to catch rounding or coercion bugs that the single provided test may miss.
